layers.process: Entry is by permit only, for authorised work purposes or visiting family living or working on the Lands. Applications need a National Police Clearance Certificate and a photograph. Transit permits are not issued to tourists or four-wheel-drive travellers. Entering without a permit is an offence for non-Aṉangu people.

own_names: Anangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara (APY) Lands; Anangu is the people's own word for themselves.
culture-and-protocol.welcome_and_acknowledgement: Entry is by APY permit only, and transit permits aren't issued to tourists or four-wheel-drive travellers. Work and consultations need written approval from the APY Executive Board or its delegate.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Don't leave established roads without consent from the appropriate Traditional Owner. Don't remove plants, animals or rocks.
culture-and-protocol.photography_and_story_permissions: Check every time with local authorities or Traditional Owners before taking photos or video; media need a permit for each entry.
culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Carry the permit; follow the Land Rights Act and the laws on alcohol on the Lands. Breaches can mean removal by SA Police.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Anangu Traditional Owners, through the APY Executive Board.

laws.rule: Entry to the Aṉangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara Lands requires an APY permit under the Aṉangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara Land Rights Act 1981 (SA). The official APY permit page asks you to apply 30 days before your visit. Applications are processed from 9 am Monday to 9 am Friday only, not on public holidays, and may take 10 to 14 days. Fees, GST included, are A$22 per person for adults and students 18 and over, and for media, and A$11 per person for children aged 6 to 17 and for student or group concession. Permits expire at the end of each financial year unless an earlier expiry is stated; renewals must be in by 30 May. Permit types on the page include general (friends or family, issued each visit), organisation or contractor, employment, media (each entry), research (each entry), and a notification form for current permit holders travelling again. As at 9 April 2025, APY will not refund the fee if a permit is refused, if weather closes the roads, if you cancel after the permit is granted, or if you cancel more than 3 working days after applying; a cancellation within 3 working days can be refunded within 10 working days.
